title: Sample preparation and image registration for correlative cryo-FM and cryo-FIB-SEM of plunge-frozen mammalian cells
protocol: Place a glass slide inside a petri dish (100 mm round dish).
Gently place the desired number of grids, carbon layer facing up, on the edge of the glass slide so that ¼ of the grid is not touching the slide.
Transfer the petri dish with the grids into a glow discharge instrument and remove the cover.
Use plasma cleaning to make the grid’s surface hydrophilic: use air (15 sccm), radio frequency power 18W, duration 2min, pulse ratio 50/255.
Take the dish out of the plasma cleaner and transfer it to a biosafety cabinet using proper aseptic techniques for working in a class II biosafety cabinet.
Prepare two glass-bottomed 35 mm imaging dishes inside the biosafety cabinet.
Place 350 μL of GM inside each glass-bottomed well (only inside the well).
Gently transfer up to four grids to each dish, carbon layer facing up.
If necessary, gently poke the grid edge with a 10 μl tip until they break the surface tension and sink.
Wash the cells twice with Dulbecco’s phosphate-buffered saline (DPBS) without calcium or magnesium.
Add 2 ml of trypsin solution to the cells and incubate for 5 min at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Check under the microscope that the cells detach; they will be round and move upon the gentle shaking of the dish.
If most of the cells are still attached, incubate for an additional minute.
Add 8 ml of growth medium (GM) to the dish, tilt it to one side and wash it several times with the same solution to aspirate as many cells as possible.
Transfer the cells to a 15 ml conical tube.
Spin at 180×g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1.5–2 ml of GM.
Remove 200 μL of GM from each dish prepared.
Add 3x10^4 cells in 200 μL of GM to the glass-bottomed area of the dish.
Shake the dish gently to spread the cells evenly on the glass bottom.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 2–4 h.
Check under the microscope that the cells have attached to the grids before adding 2 mL of growth media to each dish.
Incubate the cells for an additional 8–18 h at 37°C, 5% CO2 before proceeding.
Stain the sample right before plunge-freezing.
Wash cells 2–3 times with warm DPBS.
Incubate cells with a warm staining solution of 1 μg/mL BODIPY 493/503 in DPBS for 20 min at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Wash out the staining solution thrice with warm GM.
Transfer the cells to an incubator after washing.
Turn on the plunger and fill the humidity bath with deionized H2O.
Replace the blotting paper in the plunger.
Set the plunger parameters: Humidity: 90%. Temperature: 37°C.
Perform plunge freezing by rapidly plunging the sample into liquid cooled to cryogenic temperature.
Perform a mock test with a wet grid to determine the blot arm position parameter.
Check that the blot arm touches the grid and pushes it slightly forward.
Cool the system by pouring dry liquid N2 into the reservoir until vigorous bubbling stops, then fill the rest of the reservoir and the grid box place.
Fill the liquid ethane cup to its brim with ethane.
Pick one grid using the plunger’s tweezers when mounted properly away from the blotting paper.
Move the tweezers to the loading position and press blot to ensure a blotting mark remains on the blotting paper.
Press ‘transfer’ and gently detach the tweezers with one hand.
Hold the lower part of the tweezers with the other to keep the grid from hitting the cup.
Wear a face shield while handling the frozen samples to reduce contamination hazard from breathing.
Rapidly transfer the grid to the box.
Store the box in liquid N2 after all grids are plunged.
Start the plunger’s bake-out function to dry the plunger.
Cool every tool that touches the frozen grids to liquid N2 temperature before handling.
Clip the grids immediately after plunge-freezing, if performed.
Fix a c-shaped clip into a c-clip ring with an EM grid in it under liquid N2 using a special clipping tool and station.
Ensure cells face away from the c-clip while clipping for cryo-objective working distance (WD) considerations.
Store the grids in a liquid N2 storage system until imaging.
Turn on the operating computer and all the microscope’s components.
Wait until the computer finishes booting before turning the camera on.
Lower the cryo-objective ¾ of its range to pre-cool the objective.
Insert the pump into the liquid N2 Dewar slowly.
Allow the system 45 min to stabilize after bubbling of liquid N2 relaxes.
Turn on the LASX software and allow stage initialization while the microscope is cooling.
Open Leica’s MatrixScreener HCSA (High Content Screening Automatization) software and load the CLEM module.
Fill a dry Dewar with liquid N2 to cool the cryo-CLEM shuttle.
Bring the grid box from the liquid N2 storage.
Put the sample holder on the sample holder loading station.
Cool the shuttle in the last 5–10 min of stabilization while wearing a face shield and keeping it covered.
Transfer the grid box to the designated place in the shuttle.
Mount one grid, with its cells facing up, to the sample holder.
Grab the sample holder with the transfer rod.
Retract the rod and move away the sample holder loading station.
Cover the shuttle and attach it to the microscope.
Raise the objective slightly to avoid damage during transfer.
Open the valves of the microscope and the shuttle.
Transfer the sample.
Retract the rod.
Close the valves.
Detach the shuttle.
Lower the objective to its final position.
Find focus using brightfield.
Apply a spiral scan with brightfield and GFP to observe the grid’s condition.
Define a region in the middle of the grid, excluding areas close to the c-clip ring.
Acquire maps in all relevant channels with a step size of 1–2 μm over a range of 50–100 μm.
Go over the generated mosaic and mark cells of interest with an auto-focus point indicator.
Save a snapshot of the mosaic including all focus points for re-orientation in FIB-SEM.
Acquire a single tile stack for every cell of interest using a step size of 0.15–0.25 μm over 10 μm.
Cool the shuttle and attach it to the microscope’s stage.
Raise the objective slightly to avoid damage during transfer.
Open the valves of the microscope and the shuttle, grab the sample, retract the rod, close the valves, and detach the shuttle.
Store the grid in its box.
If another grid is to be imaged, repeat steps for defining a region, acquiring maps, marking cells, saving snapshots, acquiring tile stacks, unloading the sample, and storing grids.
Raise the objective to the maximal height.
Heat the microscope stage from the pump controller.
Turn off all components but the pump.
After reaching 60°C and drying, turn off the pump and remove it from liquid N2.
Initialize the stage and move it to the cryo-transfer position.
Cool down the microscope with liquid N2; ensure the working temperature is lower than -140°C.
Place a cryo-sample holder inside the VCM chamber.
Turn on Leica’s VCM.
Warm the VCM chamber to 50°C–70°C for one hour (optional).
Purge the enclosed space with dry N2 for 5–10 minutes before cooling it down (optional).
Fill the reservoir with dry liquid N2.
Start pumping liquid N2 to the chamber using the ‘low fill’ mode.
Pump a VCT and keep it pumped in standby.
Place the grid box inside the VCM chamber when ready.
Open the box and transfer grids onto the sample holder, cells facing up.
Cover the sample holder with its lid to prevent contamination.
Cool the pumped VCT and attach it to the VCM.
Grab the sample holder with the VCT rod and rapidly retract it to the VCT chamber.
Detach the VCT and attach it to the Crossbeam.
Coat the sample surface with a 5–10 nm conductive layer of Pt or carbon prior to loading it into the FIB-SEM.
Transfer the sample holder to the chamber.
Slide the sample holder into the cryo-stage.
Retract the sample holder slightly and turn it to remove the lid from the sample.
Detach the VCT from the crossbeam.
Close the dry N2 valve to stop the flow to the VCM.
Turn on both the FIB and the SEM columns.
Move the sample to the SEM observation position.
Adjust the working distance (WD) to the FIB-SEM coincidence point (5 mm).
Choose an object in the central area of the grid square for this adjustment.
Take a wide field of view image of the entire grid (∼100X magnification) at high resolution (at least 3027x2304 pixels).
Run SmartFIB software to operate the FIB.
Inspect the ROI with the FIB.
Adjust the stage tilt to make the ROI clearly visible at the FIB field-of-view.
Correct the WD if needed.
Increase the WD to 7–8 mm.
Open and close the nozzle of the gas-injection system for 3 cycles of 30 s each.
Depose a Pt-organometallic layer on the sample surface to protect it from damage during milling.
Move back to the working position.
Perform a milling test.
Adjust the ion dose factor and dwell time according to the sample’s properties.
Use an ion dose of (160–200 mC/cm²) for mammalian cells.
Set the typical milling current range between 50–300 pA for a slice thickness of 10–30 nm.
Cut a cross-section showing at least 2 μm of the cell in height for SEM imaging adjustment.
Optimize the SEM parameters to obtain an acceptable image quality.
Use acceleration voltage 1.6 kV, current 40 pA, pixel dwell time 12–22 μs, and pixel size 10 nm.
Set line average N=140 for detection.
Mix InLens SE and external SE2 at a ratio of 0.6–0.7 to reduce charging artifacts and optimize the signal-to-noise ratio.
Transfer the data to a third-party computer for further processing after data collection is completed.
Take out the grids and store until future use, passing through the VCM if they are to be kept.
Open the FM images.
Check the metadata.
Extract LDs center: Launch Icy.
Drag and drop the fluorescence image stack containing the BODIPY signal onto the designated area in Icy.
Check the metadata in the ‘Sequence Properties’ panel for pixel size accuracy (x and y: 0.13 μm, z: 0.15 μm).
Edit the metadata by clicking on the edit button if necessary adjustments are needed.
Delete any previously added ROI from the ‘ROI’ panel to ensure no previous data interferes with new analysis.
Use the Icy Spot Detector plugin to find LDs centers by searching for it in the search bar and selecting it.
Set the spot size to ‘Scale 2’ in the ‘Detector’ panel, ensuring associated sensitivity is set at 10.
Go to the ‘Output’ panel to export detected spots' centers to the ROI list.
Press the ‘Start Detection’ button to initiate the detection process for LDs centers.
Search for the Spot Detector plugin in the search bar.
Launch the Spot Detector plugin while keeping all default settings except for the ‘Detector’ panel.
Select 'Detect bright spots over dark background' in the detector settings.
Set the spot size to 'Scale 2'.
Adjust sensitivity to 10.
Check the box 'Export to ROI' in the 'Output' panel.
Click 'Start Detection'.
Move the z cursor on the stack to parse z and check segmentation.
Manually click LDs center of mass on the FIB-SEM stack.
Drag and drop the FIB-SEM data, here binned for memory and speed purposes.
Check the metadata in the ‘Sequence’ panel; the stack dimensions should be 40 nm in x, y, and z.
Edit the metadata by clicking on the edit button if needed.
Delete any previously added ROI (select all ROIs in the ‘ROI’ panel).
Zoom in and mark the center of the LDs with a Point 3D object.
Pick the center of the LD in z as well.
Use Point 3D objects to pick the ROIs in the ROI panel.
Import the coordinates from a .csv file if centers of LDs were found using different software.
Check the dimensions of both the source and target stacks after picking the centers of the LDs.
Adjust the parameters according to step 34 and press the ‘Play’ button to start the transformation.
Navigate in the FIB-SEM data to identify the center of LDs.
Select ‘Point 3D’ from among the ‘type of ROI’ options.
Click on the approximated center of each LD parsing the z.
Import EM ROIs from Excel using ImportRoiPointsFromFile if required.
Remove the first column and first row from the .xls file in Excel.
Save the file as a .csv file with only columns containing x, y, and z coordinates.
Open ImportRoiPointsFromFile in Icy and load your ROIs to the EM data.
Set Source image to FM with spot-detected ROIs in AutoFinder.
Set Target image to FIB-SEM with manually picked ROIs in AutoFinder.
Set Transform mode to Already in the same orientation in AutoFinder.
Set Max error to 10 μm in AutoFinder.
Set Percentage of target points to keep to 70% in AutoFinder.
Press the ‘Play’ button to initiate the AutoFinder registration.
Save the transformed source image using SaveAsTiffFast plugin for Icy.
Check that the metadata for each image opened in Icy are correct.
Edit the metadata if needed, shown in the right bar in Icy.
Delete the new xml metadata file to reset incorrect changes to original values.
Choose Affine transformation model and Isotropic noise model in eC-CLEM.
Add fiducial markers to each of the images, dragging corresponding points to match.
Rotate the field of view of an image if it helps with finding the same area in both images.
Pick the same numbered lock icon in the top left panel of both stacks for easier comparison.
Choose ‘Lock 3’ to keep the z dimension independent between datasets.
Observe orthogonal view of the image stack for better z-alignment.
Change the view from ‘2D’ to ‘OrthoViewer’ in Icy’s drop-down arrow for precise point placement.
Generate an error map in eC-CLEM after computing a transform.
Click 'Compute the whole predicted error map' to generate the map.
Adjust the histogram to scale the error map as needed.
Toggle the appearance of the scale bar or color bar under the ‘layer’ panel.
Install the histogram plugin in Icy to plot the error map distribution.
Zoom in to the fiducial points to see red lines corresponding to the error.
Measure the length of the red line using the 'ruler helper' tool to obtain the error magnitude.
Display 3D ellipse to represent the 95% likelihood of matching.
